help.title: Help
about.desc: Font Changer changes fonts and font sizes in many files at once — Word, Excel, PowerPoint, LibreOffice, RTF, HTML and CSS — and keeps everything else as it was.
start.1: Choose a folder: type its path, press Browse, or drop the folder into the window.
start.2: Set the file name mask, for example *.docx;*.pptx. A single * means all supported files.
start.3: Under “Find” enter the source font and/or size. Leave a field empty to match any font or any size.
start.4: Under “Change to” enter the new font and/or size. An empty field leaves that property as it is.
start.5: For several changes at once, add each pair to the list with “Add to list”, or load rules from a file.
start.6: Press Preview to see what would change — nothing is modified yet. Then press Change. Keep .bak backups switched on if you want to be able to go back.
formats.1: Word (.docx, .docm, .dotx, .dotm): text, styles, headers and footers, footnotes, lists and the theme fonts.
formats.2: Excel (.xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .xltm): cell fonts, rich text inside cells, comments, text boxes and the theme fonts.
formats.3: PowerPoint (.pptx, .pptm, .ppsx, .potx): slides, layouts, masters, notes, SmartArt and the theme fonts.
formats.5: RTF, and HTML / CSS: font-family, font-size, the font shorthand and <font face>. Sizes are written in points; @font-face names are never renamed.
formats.6: Not supported: PDF (its text is drawn with embedded fonts) and old binary .doc, .xls, .ppt — open them in Word or LibreOffice and save as .docx / .xlsx / .pptx first. Plain text files have no fonts.
formats.7: Font and size are matched independently: the rule “Arial 12 → Calibri 14” changes every Arial to Calibri and every 12 pt size to 14 pt, not only 12 pt Arial text. With an empty source, “any font” and “any size” are used.
formats.8: Not changed: charts, embedded objects, fonts inside pictures and embedded font files. A different font or size can change the page count and the layout, so run Preview first and keep .bak backups on.
presets.intro: Ready-made rules. Press “Use” to fill in the fields, then adapt them to your case.
presets.note: “Any font” keeps symbol fonts such as Wingdings unless you switch that option off.
preset.official.title: Official documents: Times New Roman, 14 pt
preset.official.desc: Every font becomes Times New Roman and every size 14 pt — a common requirement for official papers.
preset.arial_calibri.title: Arial → Calibri
preset.arial_calibri.desc: Replaces one font with another. Sizes stay as they are.
preset.any_arial.title: Any font → Arial
preset.any_arial.desc: Unifies all fonts. Sizes stay as they are.
preset.any_size_12.title: Any size → 12 pt
preset.any_size_12.desc: Sets the same size everywhere, including headings. Fonts stay as they are.
preset.small_up.title: Make small text bigger: 10 → 11 pt
preset.small_up.desc: Changes only the 10 pt text to 11 pt.
preset.times_georgia.title: Times New Roman → Georgia
preset.times_georgia.desc: A softer serif for screen reading. Sizes stay as they are.

start.7: The program scans the selected files and tells you which fonts and sizes they use. If there is only one font, it is shown in the field in grey; if there are several, click the field and choose from the list. Automatic scanning can be switched off and started with the “Scan” button instead.
start.8: “Save rules…” writes the list to a .fctpl template file; “Load rules…” reads it back together with the mask and the two options.

settings.title: Settings
formats.9: By default “any size” leaves sizes below 6 pt alone: that is how thin empty separator lines are usually made, and enlarging them would move the layout. Change the limit in the side panel (0 = protect nothing). A rule with an explicit source size always applies.
